{{other uses|Phoenix (disambiguation)}} {|{{Infobox ship begin}} {{Infobox ship image |Ship image= |Ship caption= }} {{Infobox ship career |Hide header = |Header caption= |Ship country= United States |Ship flag={{USN flag|1821}} |Ship name=''Phoenix'' |Ship ordered= |Ship builder=Rochester, MA |Ship laid down= |Ship launched= 1821 |Ship owner=*T&P Macy (1844) *Gardner & McCeave (1853) |Ship purchased= |Ship commissioned= |Ship decommissioned= |Ship in service= |Ship out of service= |Ship captured= |Ship fate=Wrecked 12 October 1858 |Ship struck= }} {{Infobox ship characteristics |Hide header= |Header caption= |Ship class= |Ship tons burthen=323{{sfnp|Starbuck|1878|p=540}} ([[Builder's Old Measurement|bm]]) |Ship length= |Ship beam= |Ship draught= |Ship hold depth= |Ship sail plan= |Ship propulsion= |Ship complement= |Ship armament= |Ship notes= }} |} '''''Phoenix''''', or '''''Phenix''''', was an American wooden [[whaler]], launched in 1821. She plied the [[Oceania|Pacific Ocean]] from her homeport of [[Nantucket, Massachusetts]]. She made ten complete voyages between 1821 and her loss, on her 11th voyage, in 1858. ''Phoenix'' and her captain, [[Perry Winslow]], discovered [[Winslow Reef, Phoenix Islands|Winslow Reef]], northwest of Canton, in 1851. The entire group of [[Phoenix Islands]] in the [[Oceania|South Pacific]] are named after a ship, which was active in the area in the 1820s, which may be this ship.{{sfnp|Denger|Gillaspy|1955|p=6}} ''Phoenix'' was in the Galapagos in 1835 and 1836. On 10 January 1836 the crew was ashore and left graffiti carved into rocks there. While in the Galapagos islands the crew also gathered tortoises to eat, perhaps as many as 140.{{sfnp|Grant|Estes|2009|p=86}} ==Whaling voyages== Between 1821 and 1858, ''Phoenix'' made 11 whaling voyages:[http://nmdl.org/aowv/whvoyage.cfm?VesselNumber=2187 National Maritime Digital Library: ''Phoenix''.] {| class="sortable wikitable" |- !
